read.passage: When Hessa joined her school's debating club, she was so shy that she could hardly speak in front of the class. Her teacher gave her one piece of advice: prepare a clear structure. Before every debate, Hessa wrote her position in one sentence, then listed three reasons, each with an example. She also prepared answers to the counter-arguments she expected. In hindsight, she says, that structure changed everything. 'If I hadn't learnt to organise my ideas, I would have given up after the first month,' she explains. Two years later, Hessa represented her region in a national competition. Although her team didn't win, she believes the experience was worth it. 'If I weren't so stubborn, I wouldn't have kept going,' she laughs. 'And now I'm not afraid of speaking to anyone.'
